Title: NVIDIA Explained Like You're 5

Audience: curious technology/business learners and investors seeking causal company history. Stakes survival capital, platform lock-in, export restrictions and investment valuation. Evergreen origin story with AI-demand context; hardware capability, CUDA developer ecosystem and favorable demand are competing/complementary explanations, while founder persistence is the narrative lens.
novelty_and_corpus_angle: Recurring simplified company explainer in Crayon; distinctive through wrong-chip reversal and long CUDA bet. Broad founder success is common in this channel; 966-wide semantic prevalence still uncounted.
competition: Within corpus, PayPal/Amazon/TSMC/Palantir offer company stories; external niche saturation and actual demand unmeasured.

Title: Petrodollar Explained Like You're 5
analysis: International monetary system, oil settlement and petrodollar recycling. Beginner geopolitics/finance learners ask why the dollar remains powerful and whether oil alternatives weaken it. Stakes reserve safety, borrowing costs, sanctions and oil dependency. Historical system story with contemporary de-dollarization coda. Creator angle is a self-reinforcing oil/dollar/security loop; alternative explanations include deep liquid capital markets, institutional trust, network effects and reserve valuation changes. Evergreen mechanism with news-sensitive examples, not a verified current-collapse prediction.
novelty_and_corpus_angle: Named monetary-system explainer rather than founder biography; within Crayon, finance history/scandals recur, exact corpus-wide prevalence not established. Secret-deal framing is an interpretation, not canonical history.
competition: Niche saturation and search demand unmeasured. Supplied videos include related crises, gold and Bitcoin, which are adjacent rather than direct substitutes.

Title: The Economic Secret of WW2
analysis: Sub-niche: macro-economic history and monetary regime, with an explicit anti-Keynesian argument. Audience problem: viewers who have heard that WW2 spending cured the Depression and want to know whether that is true. Stakes: how to interpret GDP, deficit spending and currency stability. Evergreen with 2026 gold-at-$5,000 hook in the close. Competing explanations are acknowledged only as the Keynesian view, set up as strawman figures (Samuelson, Truman) in dramatized dialogue; the video does not present economists who dispute the rationing/GDP framing.
novelty_and_corpus_angle: Channel-distinct in being an ideological thesis rather than a company story. Overlaps materially with the 5000-years-of-gold video (Bretton Woods peg, de Gaulle, Nixon 1971 'temporary measure that will probably last forever'), so audience overlap and duplication risk within the channel exist.

Title: 5000 Years of Gold Explained in 16 Minutes

novelty_and_corpus_angle: Channel format is typically a single-subject story; this is a long-timespan survey. Shares the Bretton Woods and Nixon beats verbatim with the WW2 and Petrodollar videos, indicating a reused narrative module across at least two videos (including the Nixon 'temporary measure' quote).
competition: Gold-history explainers are common externally; within corpus, Petrodollar (typical 1.28x), WW2 (weak), Great Depression (strong).

Title: The Wolf of Wall Street Scam Explained Like You're 5

novelty_and_corpus_angle: Standard, widely told explanation with the channel's comedy treatment; the CDS-as-life-insurance analogy and ratings-agency 'food critic' analogy are the memorable teaching devices.

Title: The Great Depression Explained Like You’re 5

Title: Ozempic Explained Like You're 5
